heading: མཆོད་བརྗོད།
translation:
Venerable Lady, who is filled with the youthful vitality of primordial wisdom,
By the mere remembrance of your feet, you cause the wanderers in suffering,
Together with the causes of their misery, to become but a mere name,
You, who act thus, are my eternal refuge throughout all my lifetimes.

heading: ཚིག་འགྲེལ།
translation:
Homage to Tārā, the swift and heroic,
Whose eyes are like a momentary flash of lightning,
She who arose from the opening of the stamens
Of the lotus-face of the Lord of the Three Worlds.

heading: ཚིག་འགྲེལ།
translation: Regarding this: To whom is the homage paid? She is the embodiment of the enlightened activity of all the victorious ones. She is the one who liberates [beings] from the karma and afflictions of cyclic existence, along with their results, through her great, immeasurable love. Because she is never negligent in connecting all beings to benefit and happiness, she is "Swift" (myur ma). Because she has unobstructed power and capability to act accordingly, she is "Heroic" (dpa' mo). Her wisdom-eye, which perceives the nature of reality, is "like a momentary flash of lightning" because it perceives without attachment or obstruction in a single instant; thus, she is the "One Possessing Wisdom." She is the Noble One who arose from the tears of great compassion—which are like the stamens and filaments opening within the lotus-flower face of the Noble Avalokiteśvara, the protector of the three worlds (the subterranean, the terrestrial, and the celestial). This is the word-commentary.

Regarding this: To whom is the homage paid? She is the embodiment of the enlightened activity of all the victorious ones. She is the one who liberates [beings] from the karma and afflictions of cyclic existence, along with their results, through her great, immeasurable love. Because she is never negligent in connecting all beings to benefit and happiness, she is "Swift" (myur ma). Because she has unobstructed power and capability to act accordingly, she is "Heroic" (dpa' mo). Her wisdom-eye, which perceives the nature of reality, is "like a momentary flash of lightning" because it perceives without attachment or obstruction in a single instant; thus, she is the "One Possessing Wisdom." She is the Noble One who arose from the tears of great compassion—which are like the stamens and filaments opening within the lotus-flower face of the Noble Avalokiteśvara, the protector of the three worlds (the subterranean, the terrestrial, and the celestial). This is the word-commentary.

heading: ཚིག་འགྲེལ།
translation:
Homage to her whose face is like the autumn moon,
A hundred full moons gathered together;
Blazing with the brilliant light
Of a thousand gathered stars.

translation:
Homage to her whose hand is adorned
With a gold and blue water-born lotus;
She whose sphere of activity is generosity, diligence, austerity, peace,
Patience, and meditative concentration.

The method of visualization is as follows: one should meditate on this Tārā, the Treasure of Intelligence, Sarasvatī, who increases the power of wisdom and causes intelligence to flourish. Her body is white like the autumn moon, and she sits in the half-lotus posture upon a lotus and moon seat. She has one face and two hands; her right hand is in the gesture of supreme generosity, and her left holds an utpala flower. Above this, from a mirror marked with the seed syllable Hrīḥ, light radiates, dispelling the ignorance of sentient beings. One should meditate on her as opening the treasure of wisdom, in which the power of the intelligence that realizes things as they are blazes forth. This is the sequence of visualization.

source: ཞེས་པ་ལ། ཡུལ་གང་ལ་ཕྱག་འཚལ་ན། སྐུ་གསེར་གྱི་མདོག་ལྟར་སེར་ལ་ཨུཏྤལ་སྔོན་མོ་ཆུའི་ནང་ནས་སྐྱེས་ཀྱི་པདྨས་ཕྱག་གཡོན་ན་རྣམ་པར་བརྒྱན་ཏེ་འཛིན་མ་འཕགས་མ་ཁྱེད། ལམ་སྦྱིན་པ། བརྩོན་འགྲུས། དཀའ་ཐུབ་ཚུལ་ཁྲིམས། ཞི་བ་ཤེས་རབ། བཟོད་པ་དང་། དེ་བཞིན་བསམ་གཏན་བཅས་ཕར་ཕྱིན་དྲུག་གི་སྤྱོད་པ་དང་བཅས་ཏེ་ཡུལ་འགྲོ་བ་རྣམས་སྒྲོལ་ཞིང་འཇུག་པའི་བྱང་སེམས་སྤྱོད་པ་རྒྱ་མཚོར་དབང་བསྒྱུར་བར་ཉིད་མ་སྟེ་མཛད་མ་ཁྱེད་ལའོ། །ཞེས་པ་ནི་ཚིག་འགྲེལ་ལོ། །
translation: "To whom do I offer homage?" It is to you, Noble Tārā, whose body is yellow like the color of gold, and whose left hand is perfectly adorned with and holds a blue utpala lotus born from the water. You are the one who possesses the conduct of the six perfections—generosity, diligence, austerity (ethical discipline), peace (wisdom), patience, and likewise meditative concentration—and who masters the ocean of bodhisattva conduct that liberates and engages the sentient beings of the world. This is the word-by-word commentary.

This is the sequence of visualization.

translation: "To whom do I offer homage?" It is to you, the Noble One, who reside in a place where you are respectfully worshipped and praised by the lord of gods, Indra, in the east; the sage Agni in the southeast; Brahmā above; Vāyu in the northwest; and the various Īśvaras, namely Yama, in the south; as well as the lord of nāgas in the west, the steadfast goddess of the earth below, and the great-handed mountain-holders. Likewise, you are the object of praise for the Noble One, Tārā, before whom there respectfully gather and offer praise those who proclaim your greatness in this world: the spirits such as the obstacles in the northeast; the zombies in the southwest, who are the truthful and excellent ones; the gandharvas, who are the retinue of Indra in the east; and the hosts of wealth-lords, such as the yakṣa Vaiśravaṇa in the north. This is the word-by-word commentary.

It is to you, the Noble One, who reside in a place where you are respectfully worshipped and praised by the lord of gods, Indra, in the east; the sage Agni in the southeast; Brahmā above; Vāyu in the northwest; and the various Īśvaras, namely Yama, in the south; as well as the lord of nāgas in the west, the steadfast goddess of the earth below, and the great-handed mountain-holders. She has one face and two arms; her right hand is in the supreme generosity mudrā, and her left holds an utpala. heading: ཚིག་འགྲེལ།
translation: Regarding this: To whom is the homage paid? It is to You, who with the fierce sound of the syllable Traṭ—which tears apart—and the sound of the syllable Phaṭ—which causes to burst—completely destroy the malevolent magical wheels of others who possess harmful intentions and practices, such as curses, evil mantras, and lightning or hail. As a sign of having transcended both existence and peace through emptiness and compassion, You trample upon the malicious ones who grasp at duality, so that they can never rise again. You blaze intensely with the fire of primordial wisdom. From the midst of the swirling, wrathful frown of Your loving affection, You are the One who makes the chains of meteoric iron and sparks of light blaze intensely. This is the word-by-word commentary.

This is the visualization sequence.

heading: ཚིག་འགྲེལ།
translation: Regarding this: To whom is the homage paid? Ture means "swift as lightning," and because You arise in the form of the Great Fearful One in order to swiftly protect beings from the dangerous defiles of deluded appearances, You are the One who completely destroys the champions of Mara—who are extremely difficult to tame—including the conceptualizations of the three poisons, the mental afflictions, the aggregates, and the Lord of Death. Your face, which resembles a beautiful lotus, is assumed in a form with a frowning expression in order to tame those who are perverse and malicious. Having done so, You are the One who slays and conquers, without exception, all enemies—the two obscurations that obstruct the path to enlightenment—within the state of the equality of the dharmadhātu. This is the word-by-word commentary.

Homage to Ture, the Great Fearful One,
Who completely destroys the champions of Mara,
Who forms a frowning expression upon your lotus face,
And slays all enemies without exception.

ཞེས་པ་ལ། ཡུལ་གང་ལ་ཕྱག་འཚལ་ན། ཏཱུ་རེ་ནི་གློག་ལྟར་མྱུར་བ་སྟེ་འགྲོ་རྣམས་འཁྲུལ་སྣང་འཇིགས་རུང་གི་འཕྲང་ལས་མྱུར་བར་བསྐྱབ་པའི་ཆེད་འཇིགས་པར་མཛད་པ་ཆེན་མོའི་སྐུར་བཞེང་པས། དུག་གསུམ་གྱི་རྣམ་རྟོག་ཉོན་མོངས་དང་ཕུང་པོ་འཆི་བདག་ལྷ་བུ་བཅས་བདུད་ཀྱི་དཔའ་བོ་ཤིན་ཏུ་གདུལ་དཀའ་བ་རྣམ་པར་འཇོམས་པར་མཛད་མ། རབ་ཏུ་མཛེས་པའི་ཆུ་སྐྱེས་དང་མཚུངས་པའི་ཞལ་ནི་ཕྱིན་ཅི་ལོག་པའི་མ་རུང་པ་རྣམས་འདུལ་བའི་ཕྱིར་ཁྲོ་གཉེར་དང་ལྡན་པའི་སྐུར་བཞེང་པར་མཛད་ནས། བྱང་ཆུབ་ཀྱི་ལམ་ལ་བར་དུ་གཅོད་པའི་སྒྲིབ་གཉིས་ཀྱི་དགྲ་བོ་ཐམས་ཅད་མ་ལུས་པ་ཆོས་དབྱིངས་མཉམ་པ་ཉིད་ཀྱི་ངང་དུ་གསོད་ཅིང་བཅོམ་པར་མཛད་མ་ཁྱེད་ལའོ། །ཞེས་པ་ནི་ཚིག་འགྲེལ་ལོ། །
[1-26] translation already produced for this document:
Regarding this: To whom is the homage paid? Ture means "swift as lightning," and because You arise in the form of the Great Fearful One in order to swiftly protect beings from the dangerous defiles of deluded appearances, You are the One who completely destroys the champions of Mara—who are extremely difficult to tame—including the conceptualizations of the three poisons, the mental afflictions, the aggregates, and the Lord of Death. Your face, which resembles a beautiful lotus, is assumed in a form with a frowning expression in order to tame those who are perverse and malicious. Having done so, You are the One who slays and conquers, without exception, all enemies—the two obscurations that obstruct the path to enlightenment—within the state of the equality of the dharmadhātu. This is the word-by-word commentary.

heading: ཚིག་འགྲེལ།
translation:
Homage to her whose fingers, in the mudrā symbolizing the Three Jewels,
Beautifully adorn her heart;
She who is graced by wheels in every direction without exception,
And who radiates a turbulent mass of her own light.

The method of visualization is as follows: This Noble One, the Heroine Who Cannot Be Defeated by Others, who destroys the exposing of the faults of opponents, has a dark red body color. She is seated in the half-vajra posture upon a lotus and moon. She has one face and two hands; her right hand is in the supreme giving gesture, and her left holds an utpala, upon which rests a blazing vajra. One should meditate that by means of a garland of sparks, she destroys the mental afflictions, the exposing of others' faults, and curses. This is the sequence of visualization.

heading: ཚིག་འགྲེལ།
translation: Regarding this: To whom is the homage paid? It is the mudrā symbolizing the Three Jewels, where the index, middle, and little fingers are raised, while the thumb and ring finger are curled with their tips touching, adorning the heart. She is the Noble One who is adorned with the ornaments of protection by the wheels of the eight and sixteen directions, which decorate the infinite beings who are in great fear. As for "radiating a turbulent mass of her own light," it means that by the light rays streaming forth to the beings to be tamed, You, the Tārā of the Teak Forest, protect them from all fears. This is the word-by-word commentary.

heading: གསལ་འདེབས་ཚུལ།

translation: The sixteen great fears are: 1. the fear of the lion of holding to morality and views as supreme; 2. the fear of the elephant of ignorance; 3. the fear of the fire of hatred; 4. the fear of the snake of jealousy; 5. the fear of the thief of wrong views; 6. the fear of the iron chains of desire and attachment; 7. the fear of the ocean of desire; 8. the fear of the flesh-eating demon of doubt; 9. the fear of the punishment of kings, which is the arrogance of secondary afflictions and violence; 10. the fear of the enemy of the wild and deceitful; 11. the fear of the demon of hypocrisy and forgetfulness; 12. the fear of the leper of shamelessness, lack of conscience, and lack of mindfulness; 13. the fear of the lack of faith and loss of spiritual friends; 14. the fear of the poverty of miserliness; 15. the fear of the thunderbolt of anger, resentment, and jealousy; 16. the fear of the loss of purpose due to laziness, heedlessness, and distraction; these are the sixteen.

The sixteen great fears are: 1. the fear of the lion of holding to morality and views as supreme; 2. the fear of the elephant of ignorance; 3. the fear of the fire of hatred; 4. the fear of the snake of jealousy; 5. the fear of the thief of wrong views; 6. the fear of the iron chains of desire and attachment; 7. the fear of the ocean of desire; 8. the fear of the flesh-eating demon of doubt; 9. the fear of the punishment of kings, which is the arrogance of secondary afflictions and violence; 10. the fear of the enemy of the wild and deceitful; 11. the fear of the demon of hypocrisy and forgetfulness; 12. the fear of the leper of shamelessness, lack of conscience, and lack of mindfulness; 13. the fear of the lack of faith and loss of spiritual friends; 14. the fear of the poverty of miserliness; 15. the fear of the thunderbolt of anger, resentment, and jealousy; 16. the fear of the loss of purpose due to laziness, heedlessness, and distraction; these are the sixteen.

heading: ཚིག་འགྲེལ།
source: ཞེས་པ་ལ། ཡུལ་གང་ལ་ཕྱག་འཚལ་ན། སེམས་ཅན་རྣམས་རབ་ཏུ་དགའ་བ་སྐྱེད་བྱེད་མཚན་དཔེའི་སྐུ་དང༌། ཀུན་ནས་བརྗིད༌ཅིང་མཛེས་པའི་དབུ་རྒྱན་ནོར་བུ་ལས་འོད་ཀྱི་ཕྲེང་བ་སྣ་ཚོགས་སྤེལ་མ་འཕྲོ་བ། གསུང་བཞད་པ་བརྒྱད་དང་ལྡན་པའི་རིག་སྔགས། ཧ་ཧཱ། ཧི་ཧི། ཧེ་ཧེ། ཧོ་ཧོའི་སྒྲ་དབྱངས་རབ་ཏུ་བཞད་པའི་སྒྲ་ཏུཏྟཱ་ར་ཡིས་བདུད་དགའ་རབ་དབང་ཕྱག་སྡེ་རིས་བཅས་པ་དང༌། རྒྱ་ལ་བློནཁྱིམ་བདག་སོགས་འཇིག་རྟེན་ཐམས་ཅད་དབང་དུ་བསྒྱུར་ནས་ཉིད་ཀྱི་གོ་འཕང་ལ་འགོད་པར་མཛད་མ་ཁྱེད་ལའོ། །ཞེས་པ་ནི་ཚིག་འགྲེལ་ལོ། །
translation: Regarding this: To whom is the homage offered? It is to You, who possess a body of major and minor marks that generates supreme joy in sentient beings, and from whose majestic and beautiful crown-ornament of jewels, various garlands of light radiate. Through the mantra of speech, which possesses the eight types of laughter—the melodic sounds of HA HA, HI HI, HE HE, and HO HO—and the sound of TUTTĀRE, You bring under Your power the maras, their retinues, and all beings in the world, including kings, ministers, and householders, and establish them in Your own state of attainment. This is the word-by-word commentary.

The sixteen great fears are: 1. the fear of the lion of holding to morality and views as supreme; 2. the fear of the elephant of ignorance; 3. the fear of the fire of hatred; 4. the fear of the snake of jealousy; 5. the fear of the thief of wrong views; 6. the fear of the iron chains of desire and attachment; 7. the fear of the ocean of desire; 8. the fear of the flesh-eating demon of doubt; 9. the fear of the punishment of kings, which is the arrogance of secondary afflictions and violence; 10. the fear of the enemy of the wild and deceitful; 11. the fear of the demon of hypocrisy and forgetfulness; 12. the fear of the leper of shamelessness, lack of conscience, and lack of mindfulness; 13. the fear of the lack of faith and loss of spiritual friends; 14. the fear of the poverty of miserliness; 15. the fear of the thunderbolt of anger, resentment, and jealousy; 16. the fear of the loss of purpose due to laziness, heedlessness, and distraction; these are the sixteen.

heading: གསལ་འདེབས་ཚུལ།
source: གསལ་འདེབས་ཚུལ་ནི། འཇིག་རྟེན་དབང་དུ་བྱེད་པའི་སྒྲོལ་མ་འཇིག་རྟེན་གསུམ་ལས་རྒྱལ་མ་འདི་ཉིད་སྐུ་མདོག་དམར་མོ། པད་ཟླའི་སྟེང་དུ་ཞབས་ཕྱེད་སྐྱིལ། ཞལ་གཅིག་ཕྱག་གཉིས། གཡས་མཆོག་སྦྱིན། གཡོན་ཨུཏྤལ་འཛིན་པའི་སྟེང་། རྒྱལ་མཚན་ལས་འོད་འཕྲོས་པས། འདོད་ལྷ་དབང་དུ་བསྡུས་པ། བཞད་པ་བརྒྱད་ལྡན་གྱི་སྔགས་སྒྲས་གཞན་འཕྲུལ་དབང་བྱེད་སྡེ་བཅས་དབང་དུ་གྱུར་པར་བསྒོམས་པ་ནི་དམིགས་རིམ་ཡིན།
translation: The method of visualization is as follows: Meditate on this Tārā who brings the world under Her power, the Victorious One over the three worlds, as having a red-colored body, seated in a half-lotus posture upon a lotus and moon, with one face and two arms. Her right hand is in the supreme generosity mudrā, and her left holds an utpala flower, upon which rests a victory banner from which light radiates, gathering the gods of desire under Her power. Through the sound of the mantra possessing the eight types of laughter, visualize that the Paranirmitavaśavartin gods and their retinues have been brought under Her power. This is the sequence of visualization.

heading: ཚིག་འགྲེལ།
translation: Regarding this: To whom is the homage offered? "A crescent moon" refers to the half-moon, and with this, her head is beautifully adorned; her body is also adorned with various precious jewels, and from all of these, white rays of light that dispel the hosts of suffering blaze intensely and radiate forth, subduing the pride and arrogance of all those in the world who are renowned as great lords. From the midst of her matted locks, which are as black as a bumblebee, the blissful Protector Amitābha resides, and from him, rays of immeasurable compassion—which are always free from the conceptualization of the three spheres—constantly radiate toward limitless sentient beings, causing the rain of all that is desired to fall, clearing away all the faults of the animate and inanimate world, and perfectly bestowing the glory of the excellence and auspiciousness of the environment and its inhabitants. This is the word-by-word commentary.

translation: The method of visualization is as follows: Tārā, who is the one who makes us victorious over the wars and obstacles of both form-possessing and formless beings, has a red-colored body. She is seated upon a lotus and moon with her legs in a half-vajra posture, with one face and two hands, and three eyes. Her face has a peaceful yet wrathful expression. Her right hand is in the supreme generosity mudrā, and above her left hand, which holds an utpala, she raises a vajra-fence. From this, rays of light and sparks of vajras blaze intensely and radiate forth, completely destroying the armies of the external enemies without remainder. Then, visualize the light rays gathering back, and all sentient beings, both oneself and others, being enclosed within the vajra-fence. This is the visualization sequence.

heading: ཚིག་འགྲེལ།
source: ཞེས་པ་ལ། ཡུལ་གང་ལ་ཕྱག་འཚལ་ན། རི་རབ་གླིང་བཞི་དང་བཅས་པའི་ས་གཞིའི་ངོས་ལ། ཟིལ་གྱིས་གནོན་པའི་རྒྱ་སྡིག་མཛུབ་ཕྱག་གི་མཐིལ་གྱིས་དྲག་ཏུ་ཡང་ཡང་སྣུན་ཅིང་། ཞབས་ཀྱིས་རྡུངས་པས། འཇིག་རྟེན་གསུམ་གཡོ་ཞིང་འགུལ་བར་མཛད་མ། ཞལ་ཁྲོ་གཉེར་གྱི་ཉམས་ཅན་དང་ལྡན་པར་མཛད་ནས། ཡི་གེ་ཧཱུཾ་གི་སྒྲ་རབ་ཏུ་སྒྲོགས་པས་འོད་ཟེར་རྡོ་རྗེའི་མེ་ཆར་དག་གིས། ས་འོག་རིམ་པ་བདུན་པོ་སྟེ། ༡ མི་མ་ཡིན་གྱི་གཞི། ༢ ལྷག་པའི་གཞི། ༣ གཞི་མེད་པ། ༤ གཞི་ཉིད། ༥ བཅུད་ཀྱི་གཞི། ༦ གཞི་བཟང་པོ། ༧ དག་པའི་གཞི་བཅས་ཡན་གྱི་གདུག་པ་ཅན་དམ་སྲི་རྣམས་ཀྱི་ནི་སྙིང་དང་མགོ་བོ་འགེམ་སྟེ་སྐྱེ་བ་མེད་པ་ཡུམ་ཆེན་མོའི་ངང་དུ་བརྒྱལ་བར་མཛད་མ་ཁྱེད་ལའོ། །ཞེས་པ་ནི་ཚིག་འགྲེལ་ལོ། །
translation: Regarding this: To whom is the homage paid? It is to Her who strikes the surface of the earth—which includes Mount Meru and the four continents—repeatedly and forcefully with the palm of Her hand in the threatening mudrā that suppresses all, and who tramples it with Her feet, causing the three worlds to shake and tremble. She assumes a wrathful, frowning expression, and by loudly proclaiming the syllable Hūṃ, She releases a rain of vajra-fire from light rays. This shatters the hearts and heads of the malevolent spirits and dam-sri demons residing upon the seven underworld levels, namely: 1) the ground of non-human spirits, 2) the ground of the superior, 3) the groundless, 4) the ground itself, 5) the ground of essence, 6) the good ground, and 7) the pure ground. She causes them to faint into the state of the Great Mother, where there is no birth. This is the word-by-word commentary.

translation: The method of visualization is as follows: visualize this Noble One, the Wrathful Frowning Tārā, who subdues the harm caused by malevolent spirits and classes of obstructors, as having a black body, seated in the half-lotus posture upon a lotus and moon. She has one face and two arms; her right hand is in the gesture of supreme generosity, and above the utpala held in her left hand, she wields a pestle and releases a rain of vajra-fire through the sound of the syllable Hūṃ. By striking the earth with her hands and feet, she destroys the malevolent spirits and dam-sri demons, transforming them into the expanse of reality; this is the sequence of visualization.

source: གསལ་འདེབས་ཚུལ་ནི། དགྲ་ཇག་ཆོམ་རྐུན་འཆིང་བའི་སྒྲོལ་མ་དཔག་མེད་གནོན་མ་འདི་ཉིད་སྐུ་མདོག་དམར་སེར། པད་ཟླའི་སྟེང་དུ་ཞབས་ཕྱེད་སྐྱིལ། ཞལ་གཅིག་ཕྱག་གཉིས། གཡས་མཆོག་སྦྱིན། གཡོན་ཨུཏྤལ་འཛིན་པའི་སྟེང་དུ། མཆོད་རྟེན་དང༌། ཐུགས་ཀའི་ཧཱུཾ་ལས་འོད་ཟེར་ཧཱུཾ་ཡིག་གྲངས་མེད་དང་། ཞབས་མཐིལ་ས་ལ་བརྡབས་པས་རི་རབ་དང༌། མནྡཱ་ར། འབིགས་བྱེད། ཁམས་གསུམ་གཡོ་བའི་སྟོབས་ཀྱིས་དམིགས་བྱ་རྣམས་ཞབས་འོག་ཏུ་མནན་པར་བསྒོམས་ནི་དམིགས་རིམ་ཡིན།
translation: The method of visualization is as follows: This Tārā, the Immeasurable Subduer who binds enemies, robbers, and thieves, has a reddish-yellow body. She sits in the half-lotus posture upon a lotus and moon disc. She has one face and two arms; her right hand is in the mudrā of supreme generosity, and her left holds an utpala flower. Upon the flower is a stūpa, and from the HŪṂ at her heart, countless HŪṂ syllables radiate. By stamping the soles of her feet upon the earth, she causes Mount Meru, Mandara, and Vindhya, as well as the three realms, to tremble. One should meditate that by this power, the objects of visualization are suppressed beneath her feet. This is the sequence of visualization.

heading: གསལ་འདེབས་ཚུལ།
translation: The method of visualization is as follows: The Noble Goddess Marīcī, who redeems the *bla* and *tshe* of the sick, is white in color, seated with legs in a half-lotus posture upon a lotus and moon disk. She has one face and two hands; her right hand is in the supreme generosity mudrā, and her left hand holds an *utpala* flower. Upon that flower, light rays radiate from a golden fish, and by this, one meditates that the stolen *bla* and *tshe* of the sick person are retrieved and regained; this is the sequence of visualization.

The method of visualization is as follows: The Noble Goddess Marīcī, who redeems the *bla* and *tshe* of the sick, is white in color, seated with legs in a half-lotus posture upon a lotus and moon disk. She has one face and two hands; her right hand is in the supreme generosity mudrā, and her left hand holds an *utpala* flower. Upon that flower, light rays radiate from a golden fish, and by this, one meditates that the stolen *bla* and *tshe* of the sick person are retrieved and regained; this is the sequence of visualization.

The method of visualization is as follows: Tārā, who is the one who makes us victorious over the wars and obstacles of both form-possessing and formless beings, has a red-colored body. She is seated upon a lotus and moon with her legs in a half-vajra posture, with one face and two hands, and three eyes. Her face has a peaceful yet wrathful expression. Her right hand is in the supreme generosity mudrā, and above her left hand, which holds an utpala, she raises a vajra-fence. From this, rays of light and sparks of vajras blaze intensely and radiate forth, completely destroying the armies of the external enemies without remainder. Then, visualize the light rays gathering back, and all sentient beings, both oneself and others, being enclosed within the vajra-fence. This is the visualization sequence.
